li.label: they stayed
li.description: They could have walked on with their own people. They stayed here instead, and I'm fairly sure I'm part of the reason.

li.label: silver for a stranger
li.description: We paid good silver for one more mouth at the table. I hope the new one can at least cook.

li.label: watched them leave
li.description: I stood at the edge of the fields until I couldn't see them anymore. Nobody asked me to come in, which was decent of them.

li.label: not wanted there
li.description: I asked those people for a place among them, and they said no. Fine. Their walls are ugly anyway.

li.label: an apology, of sorts
li.description: The worst apology I've ever heard, squeezed out through gritted teeth in front of everyone. I'm going to treasure it.

li.label: made me grovel
li.description: I was made to apologize in front of a room full of mud farmers. I won't forget whose face I was looking at.

li.label: insulted under my own roof
li.description: A guest said that to my face at my own table, and we went on passing the salt. I keep thinking of better answers.

li.label: we let guests walk on us
li.description: A visitor insulted one of ours at dinner and we all just chewed. Next time they'll take the chairs with them.

li.label: the council threw them out for me
li.description: Somebody insulted me, and their whole party got walked off our land for it. I didn't know the council had it in them.

li.label: guests driven off
li.description: One of them had a big mouth, so all of them had to pack up and walk. The rest never said a word to anyone.

li.label: sold what they left me
li.description: It was the last thing I had of them, and I sold it to a stranger. The silver spends just fine. That's the worst part.

li.label: kept the heirloom
li.description: A trader wanted it. I still have it. Some things shouldn't end up in a stranger's pack, and I'm glad this one didn't.

li.label: wouldn't sell
li.description: Wouldn't sell, not even at my price. I like that. Means they'll be hard to cheat, and worth the trying.

li.label: silver walked away
li.description: Somebody stood right there with a purse open, and we said no because of feelings. I've been through the stores. There are no feelings in them.

li.label: silver in the stores
li.description: Finally someone sold something sentimental for actual silver. You can't eat a keepsake.

li.label: my prisoner went home
li.description: I asked for a prisoner's freedom and got it. Somewhere out there someone is walking home because I opened my mouth.

li.label: soft on prisoners
li.description: We caught one, fed one, and now we've let one stroll out the gate. Next time they'll bring friends.

li.label: talked through the cell door
li.description: Three evenings by a cell door, and now I know about their mother's goat and the scar on their knee. It's hard to think of them as a prisoner.

li.label: my plea for a prisoner refused
li.description: I asked them to let a prisoner go home and they said no. I still carry the meals down. I've stopped looking through the bars.

li.label: bandaging raiders now
li.description: They came over the fields to kill us, and now we're spending good bandages on one of them. Wonderful.

li.label: one less raider
li.description: One of them asked for mercy and got it, the quick kind. Sounds fair to me.

li.label: we killed someone lying down
li.description: They were on the ground, they were begging, and we killed them anyway. I keep hearing the begging.

li.label: finished a fallen enemy
li.description: They looked at me the whole time. It was the right thing, probably. I've washed my hands three times and they still feel wrong.

li.label: left them to bleed
li.description: Someone out there was calling for help all afternoon, and we let them call. I stuffed cloth in my ears and it didn't help.

li.label: we fed the hungry
li.description: For once we were the ones with full stores, and we didn't make them ask twice. I watched them eat at the gate. Best meal I didn't have.

li.label: gave our stores away
li.description: We worked all season for that, and it walked out the gate on somebody else's back. Charity is lovely when it's somebody else's.

li.label: turned the hungry away
li.description: One of them was carrying a child who'd stopped crying. I watched them walk off from the wall. I'll be seeing that for a while.

li.label: paid for my animal's bite
li.description: We paid good silver because a stranger can't keep their fingers out of an animal's mouth. My animal did nothing wrong. Mostly.

li.label: the council stood by my animal
li.description: A guest got bitten and the council took my animal's side, which is the correct side. There have been extra treats.

li.label: bitten, then blamed
li.description: Their beast took a piece out of my hand, and somehow that was my fault. I hope it bites them next.

li.label: my animal given away
li.description: They handed my animal to a stranger to settle a bite. It got loose on the way out, and now it's out there somewhere, forgetting my voice.

li.label: the hunt is on
li.description: Something big and dangerous, near enough to smell, and we're going after it. Finally a reason to get up early.

li.label: hunting a fine animal
li.description: Finest animal I've seen in a year, and we sent hunters after it. All that muscle, headed for the butcher's table.

li.label: a predator worth taming
li.description: Everyone else sees teeth. I see the best guard animal this colony will ever have, if it doesn't eat me first.

li.label: making friends with a predator
li.description: Someone is walking up to a predator with a bucket of food. On purpose. With the council's blessing. I've moved my bed away from the door.

li.label: something watching from the brush
li.description: There's a predator denning in sight of the colony, and we've all agreed to pretend it isn't there. I count heads at dinner now.

li.label: it's mine now!
li.description: They said yes! It's mine! It almost knows its name already. I'm going to teach it everything I know, and then some things I don't.

li.label: a wild thing indoors
li.description: A wild animal in the house because a child asked nicely. Who do they think is going to clean up after it?

li.label: helping the handlers
li.description: I get to help tame it! I hold the food. Holding the food is the most important job, they said so.

li.label: not allowed to keep it
li.description: It was right there and it liked me and they said no. I wasn't even going to let it sleep in the beds. Much.

li.label: sneered at by a noble
li.description: A titled guest called my best work a pigsty, and everyone kept eating. I built the table they were eating off.

li.label: knows their place
li.description: Their builder took correction without a fuss. Rare, among frontier folk. One almost has hopes for them.

li.label: told a noble what's what
li.description: I told a person with a title exactly what their title is worth out here. My hands are still shaking, in a good way.

li.label: an insolent builder
li.description: A common builder lectured me at dinner. I have written it down, so that I may remember it precisely.

li.label: that tonic actually worked
li.description: It tasted like a swamp in a boot and I slept like the dead. I don't care what was in it. I want the recipe.

li.label: paid silver for pond water
li.description: Colored water in a pretty bottle. Some part of me knew, and I drank the whole thing anyway.

li.label: silver down someone's throat
li.description: We had a nice stack of silver this morning. Now somebody's had a drink of pond water and the trader is laughing all the way down the road.

li.label: what if it worked
li.description: It was probably water. Probably. I keep thinking about that little green bottle anyway.

li.label: my past, bought back
li.description: The council paid a stranger to forget what they know about me, and never even asked what it was. I owe them, and I hate owing.

li.label: silver for someone's secret
li.description: Good silver went to a visitor so somebody's past could stay buried. Whose past? Nobody will say. That's how you know it's a good one.

li.label: they let my past walk in
li.description: Someone from my old life told everyone at dinner, and the council could have stopped it with a purse. Good to know what I'm worth.

li.label: they scared my past away
li.description: Someone came here to sell what they knew about me and left with nothing but a fright. I didn't think anyone here would do that for me.

li.label: threatened over an old debt
li.description: I offered a fair trade and got cornered behind a storeroom for it. I know things about that one. I'll go on knowing them.

li.label: we lean on visitors now
li.description: Some of ours took a guest behind the storeroom for a quiet word. I didn't think we were that kind of place.

li.label: going after the beast
li.description: It tore into one of ours and walked off into the trees. Now it's back, and this time we're the ones doing the stalking.

li.label: they're hunting the beast
li.description: They're going out after the thing that mauled one of us. On purpose. With the same soft bodies it already knows how to open.

li.label: cooped up indoors
li.description: Days indoors because of one animal. I've counted the knots in the ceiling twice and got a different answer each time.

li.label: taming the thing that mauled us
li.description: That animal tore into one of us, and the plan is to feed it and give it a bed. I'll be sleeping with the door barred.

li.label: my nemesis will answer for it
li.description: The order's been given. Soon they'll be gone, and what they did to me goes into the ground with them. That's what I keep telling myself.

li.label: an execution on the schedule
li.description: We're going to kill a person in chains, on a schedule, between the hauling and the cooking. I know what they did. I still don't want to be awake for it.

li.label: my nemesis under our roof
li.description: The one who hurt me eats our bread a few doors from my bed. I can hear them coughing at night.

li.label: they want my nemesis as one of us
li.description: The council wants to recruit the one who nearly finished me. Give them a bed, a hoe, a seat at our table. Maybe the seat next to mine.

li.label: recruiting my friend's attacker
li.description: The one who hurt my friend is being talked into joining us. I'm supposed to say good morning to them, eventually.

li.label: my animal was sold
li.description: They sold my animal to the first stranger who asked. It slipped the rope past the fields, and now it's out there alone, and it doesn't know how.

li.label: sold my animal, at a good price
li.description: I miss the stupid thing. That was a lot of silver, though. I miss it a little less every time I count it.

li.label: my animal isn't for sale
li.description: A stranger offered good silver for my animal and it's still asleep on my feet. I didn't realize I'd been holding my breath.

li.label: a healer saw to my old injury
li.description: A stranger with warm hands and hot stones spent an hour on my old injury. It still aches. It aches differently, and I'll take that.

li.label: mud rubbed in for silver
li.description: The council paid good silver to have mud rubbed into my old injury by someone who hummed the whole time. The injury is the same. The mud is still there.

li.label: lessons from a traveling healer
li.description: A whole afternoon with a real healer, poking at things and explaining. Half of it was nonsense. I'm keeping the other half.

li.label: the healer's practice dummy
li.description: I was the lesson. Poked, prodded and pointed at all afternoon, and my old injury is exactly where it was.

li.label: it still aches
li.description: There was a healer right there, and the council decided my old injury wasn't worth the silver. It's been aching twice as hard since, which I can only take as a protest.
